source_terms: Your camera must now operate within that 180 degree arc when you set up for your new camera angles and coverage shots
item.claim: Once the action line is established it cuts the circle of possible camera positions into two halves. All subsequent camera setups for that scene must stay within the same 180 degree arc on one side of the line.

mechanism.text: The first shot fixes which side is frame left and which frame right, and fixes the directions of attention across the film space; staying on one side of the line preserves both.

scope.conditions: coverage of a scene after the first shot has established the line

caveats.text: the permitted region is a definite geometric area shown on an overhead plan, which makes the rule testable rather than a matter of taste

source_stated_remedies: set up all coverage cameras within the 180 degree arc on the near side of the established action line

positive.description: overhead plan of the arc, paired with the frames each permitted position produces

intra_source_relations.note: the arc is defined by the line
jumping the line is the violation of this rule

source_terms: you should ideally move the camera at least 30 degrees around the semicircle before you begin to frame up a new shot of the same subject
a jump cut—two shots with similar framing of the same object cut together causing a visual jump in either space or time
item.claim: Within the 180 degree arc, the camera should be moved at least 30 degrees before framing a new shot of the same subject. Below that the perspective is not considered different enough, and cutting two similarly framed shots of the same object together produces a jump cut — a visual jump in space or time.

mechanism.text: Each shot is supposed to show the audience new information, so two coverage shots too similar to one another fail that purpose and read as a jump rather than as a cut.

scope.conditions: successive coverage shots of the same subject within the arc

caveats.text: the authors hedge with ideally and at least, giving a floor rather than a value

the figure shows five views at 30 degree intervals and demonstrates that they differ; it does not show a smaller interval, so it does not establish that 30 degrees is the threshold at which difference appears

source_terms: It is the imaginary line that cuts through the area of action along talent's sight lines or follows in the direction of an object's movement.
The editor must only select shots from one side of the line unless the line is seen to change
item.claim: The action line, or axis of action, is an imaginary line running through the area of action — along the talent's sight lines, or in the direction an object moves. It establishes a 180 degree arc around the subject and dictates which side the camera may shoot from. The editor must select only shots taken from one side of it, and so maintain the established screen direction, unless the line is seen to change on screen, as when a car changes direction during a shot.

scope.conditions: assembling coverage of a scene with an established direction of action or attention

caveats.text: the source calls the line a mental guide for both directors and editors, so the editor's obligation is to select within constraints production has already fixed
the exception — unless the line is seen to change — puts the burden on the change being visible to the audience, which the source states but does not elaborate

source_stated_remedies: select shots from only one side of the line

item.claim: An imaginary line runs through the shooting location roughly where the main action occurs, known variously as the 180 degree line, the imaginary line, the action line or the axis of action. It is established by tracing the sight line of the talent within the shot, and once established it stays essentially locked in place.

scope.conditions: a scene with established sight lines between subjects

caveats.text: the authors note there are ways to alter the line while shooting coverage, without giving them in this chapter
the source offers four names for one concept without preferring any, which is a case of a field carrying divergent terminology for the same thing
